The primary efficacy endpoint was the percentage of patients with at least one new morphometric (radiographically defined) vertebral fracture at the end of treatment with abaloparatide compared to placebo. This is the standard efficacy endpoint for drugs intended to treat postmenopausal osteoporosis. X-rays of the spine were obtained for the primary efficacy endpoint at screening and Month 18.

target_moa.text: Abaloparatide is a synthetic 34-amino acid analog of parathyroid hormone-related peptide [PTHrP(1-34)] that acts as an agonist at the PTH1 receptor (PTH1R), activating the cAMP signaling pathway; when administered intermittently it has an anabolic effect on bone, increasing bone mass and strength.

Like teriparatide (Forteo), abaloparatide acts through the PTHR1 receptor and, when administered intermittently by injection, has an anabolic effect on bone, increasing bone mass and strength

The drug substance, abaloparatide, is a synthetic 34-amino acid peptide, which has 76% homology to hPTHrP(1-34), including 100% homology for the N-terminal 22 amino acids. Abaloparatide also has 41% homology to hPTH(1-34).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2%): hypercalciuria, dizziness, nausea, headache, palpitations, fatigue, upper abdominal pain and vertigo. In Study 003, rates (TYMLOS vs placebo): hypercalciuria 11% vs 9%, dizziness 10% vs 6%, nausea 8% vs 3%, headache 8% vs 6%, palpitations 5% vs 0.4%. Warnings include orthostatic hypotension, hypercalcemia (3% vs 0.1%) and hypercalciuria/urolithiasis.

detail.text: WARNING: RISK OF OSTEOSARCOMA. Abaloparatide caused a dose-dependent increase in the incidence of osteosarcoma (a malignant bone tumor) in male and female rats at systemic exposures 4 to 28 times the human 80 mcg exposure; it is unknown if TYMLOS will cause osteosarcoma in humans. Cumulative use of TYMLOS and parathyroid hormone analogs (e.g., teriparatide) for more than 2 years during a patient's lifetime is not recommended.

citations.quote: Abaloparatide caused a dose-dependent increase in the incidence of osteosarcoma (a malignant bone tumor) in male and female rats. The effect was observed at systemic exposures to abaloparatide ranging from 4 to 28 times the exposure in humans receiving the 80 mcg dose. It is unknown if TYMLOS will cause osteosarcoma in humans [see *Warnings and Precautions (5.1)* and *Nonclinical Toxicology (13.

Because of the unknown relevance of the rodent osteosarcoma findings to humans, cumulative use of TYMLOS and parathyroid hormone analogs (e.g., teriparatide) for more than 2 years during a patient's lifetime is not recommended [see *Warnings and Precautions (5.1)*].

summary.text: TYMLOS was reviewed as a new molecular entity under PDUFA V ('the Program') because the application contained a new molecular entity received after October 1, 2012; the PDUFA goal date was extended three months for review of additional immunogenicity data. No advisory committee was convened. Two prior requests for Breakthrough Therapy Designation were denied. Approval was traditional (full) approval based on Study 003; the boxed warning for osteosarcoma risk was required with enhanced post-marketing pharmacovigilance of osteosarcoma cases.

citations.quote: This NDA was reviewed under the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) V “Program” because it contains a new molecular entity and was received after October 1, 2012. The PDUFA goal date was extended by three months after we requested and received additional immunogenicity data that required more time for review. This document summarizes the Division’s recommendations on the application.

On 5/9/14 the Applicant submitted a BTD request, based on greater BMD response and safety (less hypercalcemia) in abaloparatide-treated patients compared to Forteo. This request was denied, as these data were not considered to establish a clinically significant improvement over approved therapy.

On 5/22/15 the Applicant submitted a second BTD request, citing phase 3 fracture data in addition to the benefits claimed previously. DBRUP responded that there was statistical overlap in vertebral fracture risk reduction between abaloparatide and teriparatide in study 003, and also statistical overlap with zoledronic acid and denosumab fracture data in previous studies. Thus, this request was also denied.

In addition, you will conduct enhanced pharmacovigilance of osteosarcoma cases identified among all patients currently or previously treated with abaloparatide, regardless of formulation or indication of use.
